title: `kahan_sum`, `fsum`, `sumkahan`, `favg`: classic Kahan
verdict: classic Kahan (not Neumaier); NaN with an infinite input
description: `kahan_sum` (also `fsum`, `sumkahan`) is classic Kahan summation, not Neumaier's. Merging a partial state Kahan-adds `other.value`, then `-other.err`. `favg` divides the Kahan sum by the count.
An infinite input makes the compensation `inf - inf`, so `fsum` and `favg` of `[inf, 1]` are NaN, where `sum` is `inf` (duckdb-nonfinite-aggregates).

Order class: (a) Kahan's compensated summation per state, in the order values reach it; a constant run enters as one term fl(k·x) (`KahanAdd::AddConstant`, its product not compensated); partial states merge by two compensated steps (the other's sum, then its negated error), in the order threads finish. `favg` returns value/count − err/count. (b) Kahan: |ŝ − s| ≤ (2u + O(nu²)) Σ|x_i| (Higham §4.3); the merges are compensated steps over the partials' sums and errors, which keeps that form with n counting every step (not proved here); each constant run adds up to u·k|x|, so at most (3u + O(nu²)) Σ|x_i| in all, within #85's bound for n ≥ 3. (c) The source below; duckdb-float-sum-order round 4 (`fsum` gave one result at 1, 2 and 8 threads where `sum` varied), test_kahan_sum.test (9007199254740994). (d) No order the Lean side names: a Kahan result need not be any tree sum. Four doubles −554628673.5322614, −5523426119.001462, 2.685058088631258, 34728.84084343375 give −6078020061.007821 by Kahan, while every tree sum of them is −6078020061.007822 or −6078020061.007823. Refining it needs a behaviour such as COMPENSATED or a bound-only order (any double within #85's bound). `kahan_sum`, `fsum` and `favg` are DuckDB's own functions, so no `agg.fsum` row rests on this fact.
reference: `AggFn.fsum` (`floatSum`) adds the doubles one by one in list order from +0.0; the writers that need that order exactly use `Dialect.float_sum`. NULL without values.
